/--
Context for a sub-`InfoTree`.

Within `InfoTree`, this must fulfill the invariant that every non-`commandCtx` `PartialContextInfo`
node is always contained within a `commandCtx` node.
-/
inductive PartialContextInfo where
  | commandCtx (info : CommandContextInfo)
  /--
  Context for the name of the declaration that surrounds nodes contained within this `context` node.
  For example, this makes the name of the surrounding declaration available in `InfoTree` nodes
  corresponding to the terms within the declaration.
  -/
  | parentDeclCtx (parentDecl : Name)
  | autoImplicitCtx (autoImplicits : Array Expr)
  -- TODO: More constructors for the different kinds of scopes `commandCtx` is currently
  -- used for (e.g. eliminating `Info.updateContext?` would be nice!).

Jovan Gerbscheid said:

A significant difference is that the lean core code is compiled, which makes it a lot faster at the traversal.

Or, in light of this fact: you could try to peel off in and look at the modifiers. This is a bit ad-hoc, though, and could miss some cases.

open Lean

partial def Lean.Syntax.addsInstance (cmd : Syntax) : Bool :=
  match cmd with
  | `(command| $_ in $cmd) => cmd.raw.addsInstance
  | `(Parser.Command.declaration| $mods:declModifiers $cmd) =>
    cmd.raw.isOfKind ``Parser.Command.instance
      || (mods.raw.find? (·.isOfKind ``Parser.Attr.instance) |>.isSome)
  | `(Parser.Command.mutual| mutual $cmd* end) => cmd.any (·.raw.addsInstance)
  | _ => false

One thing you could just do is stop once you find the first BodyInfo:

let trees ← getInfoTrees
for tree in trees do
  let res := tree.foldInfoM (m := Except Name) (init := ()) fun ctx info () => do
    match info with
    | .ofCustomInfo i =>
      if let some _ := i.value.get? Term.BodyInfo then
        if let some parent := ctx.parentDecl? then
          throw parent
    | _ => pure ()
  let .error nm := res | continue
  unless Meta.isInstanceCore (← getEnv) nm do continue
  logInfo nm

This should be quite fast since the BodyInfo comes before all the stuff in the body

So, the issue there is that linters lint the whole command, and cmdSyntax includes the syntax set_option linter.impossibleInstance false in ...; the setting of options inside command elaboration is not meant to propagate to linters. Getting the linter value like that would only detect if the set_option had occurred as a separate command, earlier. So this is expected.

This is what you'd use withSetOptionIn in your linter for: it descends through set_option ... in syntax and actually elaborates those options, handing off the inner syntax to your linter with the options set in the state, so that then checking the option value within withSetOptionIn would include linter.impossibleInstance false.

The bug is that withSetOptionIn actually fully re-elaborates the syntax, including modifying the infotrees (which linters shouldn't do; they should just observe the infotrees). This creates new info nodes that don't live underneath a context info node, and infotree API often panics if the nodes we're looking at don't live underneath such a node.

Robin Arnez said:

One thing you could just do is stop once you find the first BodyInfo

Ah yes, this is probably a sensible approach! :) One tweak is that we should probably still get a list of decls to handle mutual blocks; avoid descending, but still keep looking laterally. Something like

partial def getTopLevelDeclsByBody : InfoTree → List Name :=
  go none []
where
  go (ctx? : Option ContextInfo) (acc : List Name) : InfoTree → List Name
    | context ctx t => go (ctx.mergeIntoOuter? ctx?) acc t
    | node i ts => Id.run do
      if let .ofCustomInfo i := i then
        if i.value.typeName == ``Lean.Elab.Term.BodyInfo then
          if let some decl := ctx?.bind (·.parentDecl?) then
            return decl :: acc -- don't descend into `ts`
      ts.foldl (init := acc) (go ctx?)
    | hole _ => acc

/-- Find the first instance declaration name in the info trees of the current command.
    This uses `Except` for shortcuirciting (we `throw` the value we want to have). -/
def getFirstInstanceName : CommandElabM (Option Name) := do
  for tree in ← getInfoTrees do
    let res := tree.foldInfoM (m := Except Name) (init := ()) fun ctx info () => do
      match info with
      | .ofCustomInfo i =>
        if let some _ := i.value.get? Term.BodyInfo then
          if let some parent := ctx.parentDecl? then
            throw parent
      | _ => pure ()
    let .error nm := res | continue
    unless Meta.isInstanceCore (← getEnv) nm do continue
    return some nm
  return none
